# 3 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Divine Deliverance of the Jews

---

**1** And so, in this very way, the God who watches over all things, the Father of all mercy, delivered the people of Israel from the danger they faced.

**2** Eleazar had not stopped praying, and now God answered him.

**3** Just as the elephants that had been released against the Jews were closing in and about to trample them underfoot,

**4** Ptolemy looked up and saw two glorious angels of terrifying appearance descending from heaven, visible to everyone except the Jews themselves.

**5** The Jews were filled with fear and trembling as they stood there while the elephants thundered toward them, and the angels turned the elephants back and drove them straight at Ptolemy's own troops.

**6** The crazed beasts trampled and crushed many of his soldiers and turned back against his own army.

**7** When Ptolemy saw what was happening, he was seized with terror and began to shake.

**8** He repented of his evil scheme and turned away from the wickedness he had planned.

**9** Meanwhile the Jews were bursting with joy and confidence, because God had heard their prayer.

**10** They praised their holy God and their Savior, and broke into celebrations and songs of praise.

**11** They glorified the mercy of God and praised him who had appeared in this way on their behalf.

**12** And now the king was ready to hear the praises of those he had intended to destroy.

**13** He gathered together his Friends and his council and said: You have all witnessed how much the Jews trust in their God and how he has delivered them even from death itself.

**14** Tell me honestly: is there any among you who does not acknowledge that God is watching over these people?

**15** When the king said this, the wiser among his Friends fell at his feet and acknowledged the power of the God of Israel, whose might had been demonstrated to them.

**16** The king then called for the high priest Shimon and the Jewish leaders to come before him.

**17** He said to them: Do not be afraid; take courage, for I have heard your prayer to your God and I have repented of what I was doing.

**18** I have been moved by the mercy of God to set you all free.

**19** You shall return to your homes and no one will trouble or harm you.

**20** Each of you will receive letters from me addressed to the various communities, so that you can return home in safety.

**21** He then had letters prepared and sent to all the governors and officials throughout Egypt, commanding them to release the Jews and to treat them with respect.

**22** And so the Jews were set free from all their suffering.

**23** They returned home in great joy, singing hymns of thanksgiving to the God of Israel who had saved them.

**24** All who had helped them during their ordeal rejoiced with them.

**25** The king returned to his palace full of joy and gave thanks to God.
